text:
**Key component price findings for the single-joint test rig:**

### Servo Actuator (2026)
- **MG996R** (11 kg·cm metal gear, analog; classic budget/high-value hobby servo): ~$5–$9 (for a name-brand or tested clone; multipacks can go lower per unit, genuine closer to $9).
- **ANNIMOS DS3218** (20 kg·cm digital, metal gear, waterproof): ~$15–$18.
- **High-torque servos** (ANNIMOS DS3235, 35 kg·cm+): ~$22–$30 per unit.
  - [Source: Best Servo Motors for Robotics 2026](https://microcontrollerslab.com/best-servo-motors-robotics-embedded-buying-guide/) (July 2026 review, prices live on Amazon and similar marketplaces.)

### Load Cell (2026)
- For force/torque measurement in a test rig, the usual choices are single-point (~0.3–100 kg; aluminum, cheapest) or S-type/shear-beam (up to several tons) for more versatility.
- **Single-point aluminum cell (0.3–10 kg):** $12–$25 for basic units without calibration or certificate.
- **S-type/shear-beam (10–100 kg, alloy steel):** $25–$45 for standard analog output.
- **Digital/industrial cells:** $50–$200 and up (not needed for student/bench test-rig).
- [Source: SpecForge Load Cell Price 2026](https://www.sourcebyspec.com/news/load-cell-price-2026-cost-drivers-sensor-classes-and-tco.html)—summary: plan $15–$40 for an analog cell, 1.5–2.5× once you include bridge board, indicator, mounting.

### Microcontroller (2026)
- **Official Arduino Uno R4:** $20 (Minima); $27.50 (WiFi). [Source](https://electricalflux.com/mcu-boards/arduino-uno-cost-official-vs-clone-pricing)
- **Premium clone (e.g., Elegoo):** $11–$14.
- **Budget clone:** $4.50–$7.
- **ESP32/compatible board:** Often $5–$12, with WiFi and more IO if needed.

---

## Single-Joint Test-Rig Proposal (draft)

Will now draft a markdown proposal with use-case paragraph, BOM, capability rationale, and link all figures to the sources above.
